info.title: LinktoDM API
info.description:
The LinktoDM API lets you list your connected channels, read and update
your contacts, manage custom fields, and send direct messages from your
own tools and integrations.

## Authentication

Two credentials are accepted.

**API key** — generate one in the LinktoDM dashboard under
**Settings > API** and send it on every request in the `X-API-Key`
header. The full key is shown only once at creation — store it securely.
Keys can be revoked at any time from the same page. API keys carry every
permission.

**OAuth 2.0** — for applications acting on a user's behalf. Send the
access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Tokens are issued by the
authorization code flow at `/v1/oauth/authorize` and `/v1/oauth/token`,
last one hour, and are renewed with the accompanying refresh token.
Available scopes are `contacts:read`, `contacts:write`, `messages:send`
and `webhooks:manage`; a request outside the granted scopes returns
`403`. Contact us to register an application.

API access requires the **Pro+** plan on either credential — a caller on
a lower plan receives a `403`.

## Rate limiting

Requests are throttled per key. When you exceed the limit you receive a
`429` with a `Retry-After` header (seconds).

## Channels

`GET /v1/channels` lists the Instagram accounts and Facebook pages
connected to your workspace. Channels are connected from the LinktoDM
dashboard — they cannot be created via the API. Use a channel's `id`
(`ig-<id>`, `ig-business-<id>` or `fb-page-<id>`) as the `channel_id`
filter on other endpoints.

## Contacts

Contacts are created by the messaging platform when someone messages
your connected account — they cannot be created via the API. `name`,
`username` and `picture` are re-synced from the platform and therefore
read-only; writable fields are `email`, `phone_number` and custom field
values. **Deleting a contact is permanent** and removes its tags and
custom field values.

Contact list and get responses include `custom_fields`: one object per
live custom field (`slug`, `name`, `value`), oldest first. `slug` is the
stable key; `name` is the display name. `value` is the canonical text
stored for that contact — the same string as `fields[slug]` — or `""`
when the contact has no value. Array fields keep that stored text.
`fields` (slug to text, stored values only) is unchanged. Soft-deleted
fields are omitted.

## Sending messages

`POST /v1/contacts/{contact_id}/send_message` returns `202` when the
message is queued — delivery itself is asynchronous through per-channel
rate-limited queues. Meta only permits messages within **24 hours of
the contact's last inbound message**; a send outside that window is
accepted by this API but rejected by the platform. Pass an
`Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe.

get.description:
List the connected channels (Instagram accounts and Facebook pages).

Channels are connected from the LinktoDM dashboard — they cannot be
created via the API. Use each channel's `id` as the `channel_id`
filter on other endpoints.

The account this credential belongs to.

Doubles as the connection test for integrations: a `200` means the
credential is valid, the plan allows API access, and the account is
reachable. No scope is required — a connection must be testable
whatever it was granted.

List contacts with their tags and custom field values.

Newest first by default, so polling for recent contacts works without
paging through the whole list. `fields` is the slug-keyed map of stored
values. `custom_fields` lists every live custom field (`slug`, `name`,
`value`), with an empty `value` when the contact has not set it.

get.description:
Fetch one contact with its tags and custom field values.

`custom_fields` lists every live custom field for the account
(`slug`, `name`, `value`). `value` matches `fields[slug]` when set
and is empty otherwise.

patch.description:
Update a contact's email, phone number and custom field values.

`name`, `username` and `picture` are read-only — they are re-synced
from the messaging platform. Custom field values go in `fields`
keyed by slug; a null value clears the field.

delete.description:
Permanently delete a contact with its tags and custom field values.

This cannot be undone. If the person messages the account again, a
fresh contact is created by the platform sync.

post.description:
Add tags to a contact.

Idempotent — adding a tag the contact already has is a success, not a
conflict, so a retried request behaves the same as the first.

Remove tags from a contact.

A POST rather than a DELETE with the tag in the path: tag names are
free-form and may contain `/` or `#`, which a path segment cannot
carry safely. Removing a tag the contact does not have is a no-op.

get.description:
Every tag in use across your contacts, alphabetically.

Powers the tag dropdowns in connected integrations.

post.description:
Queue a text message to a contact (202 = accepted for delivery).

Delivery is asynchronous through per-channel rate-limited queues.
Meta only allows messages within 24 hours of the contact's last
inbound message; sends outside that window are accepted here but
rejected by the platform.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Optional. Requests with the same key are de-duplicated for about an hour, so a timed-out request can be retried without double-sending.
schema.title: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: Optional. Requests with the same key are de-duplicated for about an hour, so a timed-out request can be retried without double-sending.

post.description:
Create a custom field definition. The slug is generated from the
name and immutable afterwards.

patch.description:
Update a custom field's name, description or folder (slug and type
are immutable).

delete.description:
Delete a custom field definition. Existing values are kept in
place, so restoring the definition restores the data.

post.description:
Start receiving an event at your endpoint.

Re-registering an identical subscription returns the existing one
rather than creating a duplicate, so retries are safe.

get.description: List your registered endpoints, including deactivated ones.

delete.description: Stop receiving an event. Takes effect on the next event.

get.description:
Recent contact events, newest first.

Returns exactly what a webhook delivery would contain, so this can be
used to preview an event shape or to backfill after downtime.

ContactEventEnvelope.title: ContactEventEnvelope
ContactEventEnvelope.description:
One event, in the shape delivered to webhooks.

`GET /v1/events` returns exactly this, so the sample records a user
sees while building an automation match what arrives at runtime.

ContactFieldType.title: ContactFieldType
ContactFieldType.description: Data type of a custom contact User Field.

ContactUpdate.title: ContactUpdate
ContactUpdate.description:
Writable contact fields. Platform-synced fields (name, username,
picture) are rejected — any unknown key is a 422.

CustomFieldUpdate.title: CustomFieldUpdate
CustomFieldUpdate.description: Slug and type are immutable so saved flows keep working.

EventChange.title: EventChange
EventChange.description: Which part of the contact moved, and from what to what.

PublicAccount.title: PublicAccount
PublicAccount.description:
Who the current credential belongs to.

Deliberately free of anything secret. Zapier renders
`connection_label` next to the connected account in a user's app
list, and its review guidelines forbid showing API keys, secrets or
long opaque ids there.

PublicChannel.title: PublicChannel
PublicChannel.description:
A connected messaging channel (Instagram account or Facebook page).

``id`` is the channel id used elsewhere in the API, e.g. the
``channel_id`` filter on ``GET /v1/contacts`` — formats: ``ig-<id>``,
``ig-business-<id>``, ``fb-page-<id>``.

custom_fields.title: Custom Fields
custom_fields.description: Live custom fields for this account, oldest first. `value` is the canonical text (the same string as `fields[slug]`), or empty when this contact has no value. Deleted fields are omitted.

slug.title: Slug
slug.description: Stable key. Unchanged when the field is renamed.

value.title: Value
value.description: Canonical text stored for this contact. Empty when unset. Array fields use that stored text, the same string as `fields[slug]`, not a joined export string.

PublicContactCustomField.title: PublicContactCustomField
PublicContactCustomField.description: One live custom field and this contact's value for it.

TagNames.title: TagNames
TagNames.description:
Tags to add to, or remove from, a contact.

Add and remove are separate operations rather than a replace-set: a
replace would silently strip tags the caller never mentioned, which
is a data-loss trap when LinktoDM's own flows are writing tags at the
same time.

event_type.title: Event Type
event_type.description: One of the documented event types, e.g. `contact.tag_added`.

target_url.title: Target Url
target_url.description: HTTPS endpoint that will receive the POST.

tag_name.title: Tag Name
tag_name.description: Only for tag events — restrict to a single tag.

field_slug.title: Field Slug
field_slug.description: Only for `contact.field_set` — restrict to one custom field.

event_name.title: Event Name
event_name.description: Only for `flow.custom` — the event name given to a Send to Zapier action inside a flow.

WebhookSubscriptionCreate.title: WebhookSubscriptionCreate
WebhookSubscriptionCreate.description:
What a consumer sends to start receiving an event.

Zapier calls this from `performSubscribe`, passing its own
`bundle.targetUrl` and whichever filter the user picked in the trigger
setup.
